name: Juvelook

lead: Juvelook is a poly-D,L-lactic acid (PDLLA) injectable from VAIM Inc. of Seoul, used by clinicians as a skin booster and collagen stimulator under the eyes, in nasolabial folds, forehead, cheeks, clavicle and pores. People use it for smoother tear troughs, softer folds and better skin texture.

PDLLA is described as a biostimulator that prompts the body to produce collagen over time, so skin thickens and firms. Published reports describe a PDLLA and hyaluronic acid hybrid, with variants named Juvelook Volume and Juvelook GLAM. The literature is mainly small studies, case series and case reports, plus animal research.

paras: A clinician injects it, usually in a short series of sessions, with improvement building gradually as collagen forms.
Reported problems include firm nodules after tear trough injection, and a rabbit study examined accidental intra-arterial injection. It is performed by trained clinicians.

angle.text: People use Juvelook to smooth tear troughs and folds and improve skin texture. The PDLLA stimulates collagen so skin thickens and firms over time. Support comes from small studies and case reports.

lead: Juvelook is an injectable poly-D,L-lactic acid (PDLLA) product made by VAIM Inc. of Seoul, South Korea, used in aesthetic medicine as a skin booster and collagen-stimulating agent. Published reports describe a PDLLA and hyaluronic acid hybrid formulation, with variants named Juvelook Volume and Juvelook GLAM.[1][2][3]

Published literature consists mainly of case reports, case series and small clinical studies, including use in the tear trough, nasolabial folds, forehead, sunken cheeks, clavicle and facial pores, as well as animal research and case reports of complications such as nodules.[4][1][5][6][7][3][8]
infobox: Tear trough, nasolabial folds, forehead, cheeks, skin texture

paras: Studies have examined Juvelook for lower eyelid or tear trough rejuvenation in Korean women,[1] nasolabial fold correction,[8] lateral sunken cheek (subzygomatic depression),[7] clavicular augmentation using a cannula,[3] forehead augmentation combined with autologous fat transfer,[6] and, in a case series, facial pore reduction with microneedling and topical application.[5]

A 2025 study evaluated the efficacy and safety of Juvelook for tear trough deformities in Korean women.[1] A case series of microneedling combined with topical Juvelook assessed pore size and skin texture.[5] A study on forehead augmentation evaluated 12-month safety, efficacy and volume stability of sequential PDLLA and fat transfer.[6] Further reports address subzygomatic depression, nasolabial folds and clavicular augmentation.[7][8][3]

A case report used ultrasound and radiological patterns to assess collagen stimulation and tear trough enhancement,[9] and a study compared pain between the left and right sides during skin-booster injection.[10] Most of these are small, uncontrolled or case-level evidence.

A case report described a 42-year-old woman who developed firm, non-inflammatory nodules about three weeks after PDLLA injection in the tear trough; the nodules were managed with a monopolar radiofrequency device.[4]
A 2026 rabbit ear study investigated vascular behaviour and tissue response after intra-arterial injection of Juvelook and Juvelook Volume.[2] Animal findings do not establish human risk rates.
